title.narrative: Towards Ending AIDS as a Public Health Threat by 2030

description.narrative: Towards Ending AIDS as a Public Health Threat by 2030.The Global Fund’s support contributes to the achievement of the overall strategic goal of the Zimbabwe National HIV and AIDS program to end AIDS as a Public Health threat (aligned to SDG3) by 2030. To reach this goal, Zimbabwe aims at achieving the following impact results: reduce HIV incidence in Zimbabwe by 60% from 0.48% in 2018 to less than 0.19% by 2026; to reduce AIDS-related deaths to 60% from 21,800 in 2018 to less than 10,464 in 2026

title.narrative: YP-4 Number of high-risk adolescent girls and young women who received any PrEP product at least once during the reporting period

description.narrative:
"Indicator Description: This indicator assesses the availability and uptake of PrEP among high risk AGYW 15-24 Years. Eligibility should include at a minimum: 1) HIV-negative status and 2) no signs and symptoms of acute HIV. 3) the third criteria, whether an individual is at substantial risk for HIV and may benefit from PrEP, will be contextual and should be based on national guidelines. Programme Implementation Modalities: S2S mentors, offer information , education and communicate with clients on SRHS, HTS, pre-test counselling, comorbidity supply, mental Health and Psychosocial Support- screening and management of mental health disorders, adherence support and link the high risk AGYW to MOHCC or local council clinics. Baseline: According to the 2022 DHIS2 data the total number of AGYW 15-24 recieved PrEP in the 25 GF supported districts was 3,222. Target: Target were set in an increamental basis based on the current performance. Using the GF resources 15%, 20% and 25% of the AGYW reached with defined package of programme will be enrolled for PrEP. Therefore, the target will be 3,939 in 2024: 5,253 in 2025 and 6,566 in 2026. The implementation is the same as the GF districts listed in Y-P2 indicator. This indicator will report only on GF funded 25 districts, and will exclude PEPFAR and NATF. Numerator: Number of high risk AGYW 15-24 prescribed or dispensed any form of PrEP at least once during the reporting period. Individuals prescribed different PrEP products or regimens at different times, either event-based or ongoing, during the reporting period should be counted only once.
The reported data will be disaggregated by newly initiated on PrEP, PrEP re-supply and re-started on Prep. Disaggregation by PrEP product (oral PrEP, injectable PrEP); Age (15-19, 20-24, 25+); Data Source: Facility PrEP Registers (and triangulated with program monitoring tools). Data Source: PrEP register fed in to DHIS2. Limitation: The reported data will not directly measure attribution of the GF contribution, because all districts are not covered by the GF programme but PrEP is being provided by MOHCC as part of the routine health service programme provision. "

title.narrative: HTS-3c Percentage of sex workers that have received an HIV test during the reporting period in KP-specific programs and know their results

description.narrative:
"Indicator Description: The indicator measures progress made in providing HIV testing services to members of the Key Populations specifically Sex workers (SW). Baseline: At baseline, the denominator in 2022 was 26,010, the number reached for both PEPFAR (10,271) and GF 5,140) (annual performance divided by 2) hence numerator was 30823/2. This was 59.25% coverage of population size estimate in 2022. To note that as per GC7 guidance, non-cumulative other is the recommended cumulation type but the country / NAC system currently can only use ""non cumulative special"" as reporting. A Management Action will be part of the grant agreement to support the country/implementers to transition to non-cumulative other reporting. Target: The HIV negative population size estimate has been revised to 44,754 (86,066 i.e. total sex worker size estimate in 41 districts with SW programme from the AMETHIST study with 48% HIV prevalence. The targets were set as 22,774 for PEPFAR and this was flat lined throughout the three years. For GF the target was based on tests done. Hence targeted sex workers for 2024 is 40,279 (PEPFAR 22,774 + GF 17,505) i.e 90%, 2025 is 41,398 i.e 92.5% (PEPFAR 22,774 + GF 18,624) and in 2026 is 42,517 (PEPFAR 22,774+ GF 19,743) i.e 95% coverage from the total PSE of HIV negative population in the 41 districts. In ZNASP IV Addendum, the targets were set as 95% from 2024 onwards. However, considering the revised PSE, this will be ambitious. Reporting will be from all partners implementing SW programme. Targeted Districts: In NFM3 there were 12 static sites: Harare, Bulawayo, Mutare, Masvingo, Gweru, Karoi, Chirindu, Victoria Falls, Beitbridge, Forbes, Chinhoyi, and Kadoma, and 36 outreach sites dotted across the country. In GC7, GF and PEPFAR are implementing SWs program in 41 districts out of 63 districts in the country. There are overlaps in 16 /41 high volume districts. PePFAR and other implementing partners are in 9 districts while GF is in 25 districts. GF will support MoHCC health care workers to provide services to sex workers in 8 transition districts. To achieve the set target the program will increase the number community cadres (microplanners) to increase coverage at a ratio of 1:60 per set semester target.GF will fund empowerment resource groups (ERG) in 10 districts for the active engagements of sex workers in sex worker led self help groups. The ERGs will build community ownership and sustainability to ensure community led service provision within the district.
Funding will maintain the coverage of the 41 priority districts through 13 static sites (including the 4 cross-border initiative sites), 36 outreach sites, and 4 drop-in centers. Data Source for reporting: Programme data for numerator and PSE for denominator.
Numerator: Number of sex workers who have been tested for HIV during the reporting period and who know their results. Denominator: Estimated number of sex workers in KP-specific program areas. Disaggregation: The indicator will be disaggregated by age (15-19, 20-24, 25+); Gender (female,male,transgender).
The denominator for disaggregated results is the number of sex workers in 15-19, 20-24 and 25+ age groups. Further disaggregation will be by institution , province, district and HIV test status (positive, negative). Data Source: Facility HTS Registers (and triangulated with program monitoring tools).
NB: The PSE for key population is currently being carried out and when reporting for the this indicator the denominator will change each subsequent year based on published latest estimates then; and those current figures will be used as denominators.
HIVST will not be included for reporting, but the PR will report on the HTS cascade in the comment section of the PU."

title.narrative: TCS-10 Percentage of pregnant women living with HIV who received antiretroviral medicine to reduce the risk of vertical transmission of HIV

description.narrative: Percentage of pregnant women living with HIV who received antiretroviral medicine to reduce the risk of vertical transmission of HIV."Indicator Description: The indicator measures the provision of ART to HIV positive pregnant and lactating women during the MTCT risky period in line with current WHO Guidelines. The national strategy aims to scale up life-long ART for all pregnant and lactating women, towards elimination of new paediatric infections. Baseline: The programme used HIV estimates of 2022 and it shows an increase in the ART coverage of women receiving ARVs at 84.5% . Targets: The targets were informed by the programme performance trend analysis. Zimbabwe is one of the countries aiming to be validated by 2025, hence the country has set ambitious targets to meet the global validation targets for process indicators of >= 95%.The targets are inline with ZNASP IV Addendum (2024-2026) of increasing the HIV positive pregnant women on ART at 90% in 2024, 93% in 2025 and 95% in 2026. PEPFAR is providing additional support to 44 districts. The recent introduction of user fees will affect pregnant women's access to PMTCT services. Hence a component has been added under Community-Led research looking at the effect of user fees on HIV and TB services. Numerator: Number of pregnant women living with HIV who delivered during the past 12 months and received antiretroviral medicines during pregnancy to reduce the risk of vertical transmission of HIV. Denominator: Estimated number of women living with HIV who delivered within the past 12 months (derived from HIV estimates) Source of Data: Program facility records including ANC and ART Registers compiled into Monthly Return Forms submitted through DHIS2. During reporting, data will be disaggregated by risk period: a) booked already on ART, b) initiated in ANC, and c) Labour & delivery and Post-delivery. Sources for reporting: DHIS2"

title.narrative: RSSH/PP M&E-1 Completeness of reporting: Percentage of expected monthly reports (for the reporting period) that are actually received

description.narrative:
"""Indicator Description: The indicator measures completeness of facility reporting: Percentage of submitted facility monthly reports (for the reporting period) that are received per the national guidelines. Completeness reporting is defined according to the country's national guidelines for reporting. There are currently 1800 HFs expected to be reporting monthly to district level. The form used for this indicator is Monthly Return Form which has all HIV biomedical/treatment/care service data.The numerator and denominator when reporting will use the actual HFs that are expected due to changes in sites (open and other close) during a given reporting period. Source of Reporting: DHIS2
Baseline: Based on the MOHCC 2022 annual report, 18,156/20,538 complete reports recieved from all health from the 1740 Health Facilities expected to be reporting monthly to district level. Please Note: there are still several issues that are affecting reporting. These are: 1. Electricity load shedding and unavailability of backup power options in some parts of the country. 2. Availability of the internet remains a challenge in some parts of the country with some officers having to come to work in the evening. 3. The reporting coverage remains low among private for-profit health facilities and institutions that belong to the security sector. Target: The number of reporting facilities is expected to rise to all the 1800 facilities in country. The target is to have at least 95% (1710) of these public facilities reporting every 6 months (17100 *6 = 10,260 reports) out of 10,800 expected reports. Numerator: Number of expected monthly reports (for the reporting period) that are actually received. Denominator: Total number of expected monthly reports for the reporting period. The numerator and denominator when reporting will use the actual HFs that are expected due to changes in sites (open and other close) during a given reporting period. Source of Reporting: DHIS2.
"

title.narrative: HTS-5 Percentage of people newly diagnosed with HIV initiated on ART

description.narrative: "Indicator Description: The program aims to strengthen linkage of newly diagnosed HIV clients to ART services. This provides information on proportion of people starting treatment following HIV-positive diagnosis. Baseline: The baseline was derived from the 2022 program data which shows out of 79,634 people who were newly diagnosed with HIV in 2022, 72,405 were linked to care and treatment. This translates to 90% linkage rate which was used as the baseline. Target: In line with ZNASP IV Addendum 2024 to 2026, the program aims to improve on linkage to ART of HIV positive clients from 90% in 2022 to achieving 95% from 2024 and maintainin this to 2026. The numerator targets are 79,702 (2024), 76,696 (2025), and 76,666(2026). Numerator: Number of people newly diagnosed with HIV during the reporting period who started ART. Denominator: Number of people newly diagnosed with HIV during the reporting period. The denominator is derived from targeted tests of a total of 1,677,956 (2024), 1,614,652(2025) and 1,614,000 (2026) where the number of new HIV positive tests (positivity) was generated by applying a 5.0% (2024), 5.0% (2025) and 5.0% (2026) yield to the targeted tests to give a total of 83,898, 80,732 and 80,700 newly HIV diagnosed clients for 2024, 2025 and 2026 respectively The numerator and denominator will be generated from program data once testing has been done and positives established. This data is routinely being reported and extracted from the DHIS2 system. The numerator will be generated by aiming a linkage rate of 95% for 2024, to 2026. Disaggregation: Age (<15, 15+);Gender | Age (female 15+, male 15+). Source of reporting: HTS register uploaded into the MoHCC DHIS2."

title.narrative: VT-2 Percentage of HIV-exposed infants receiving a virological test for HIV within 2 months of birth

description.narrative: "Indicator Description: The indicator measures progress to which infants born to HIV-positive women are tested within the first 2 months of life to determine their HIV status and eligibility for ART. Baseline: Based on MOHCC programme data, 47,935 infants received a virological HIV Test out of 51,845 (92.5%) pregnant women living with HIV giving birth. The data used for baseline for 2022, noted double counting in data as number os samples were being counted instead of infants. The programme has started rectifying this anomaly by introducing an updated Lab request form separating the reason for testing as initial at birth, initial at 6-8 weeks, initial at > 2 months and repeat tests at 6 weeks and any time after. This will enable the programme to distinguish the different tests done at different time points in the LIMS system. Targets: As a result the programme has maintained Early Infant Diagnosis targets for 2024, 2025, 2026 at 85%, 87%, 90% respectively. The targets are aligned to the ZNASP IV Addendum Results Framework 2024 – 2026. The programme has decentralised convectional EID testing Laboratories to make sure that all DBS samples collected for all exposed infants will be quickly tested and results return in less than 4 weeks to the facilities. Numerator: Number of HIV exposed infants born during the reporting period who received a virological HIV test within two months of birth. Denominator: Number of HIV-positive pregnant women giving birth in the last 12 months (proxy measure for infants born to HIV-positive women). Disaggregation: HIV test status (positive, negative, indeterminate) and testing platforms. Source for reporting: Laboratory Management System for all samples tested using convectional machines and DHIS2 for all POC tests done (Numerator) Denominator: HIV Annual Estimates - From EPP spectrum."
